questions.stem: The Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) is classified as a 'Retrovirus'. What unique capability defines a retrovirus?

options.option_text: It uses the enzyme reverse transcriptase to convert its RNA into DNA inside the host cell
It can survive indefinitely in a dormant state outside a host organism
It exclusively attacks the red blood cells of the host
It replicates by physically dividing itself rather than hijacking the host cell's machinery

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Most living organisms store genetic information in DNA, which is transcribed into RNA, which then makes proteins. A Retrovirus (like HIV) works backwards (retro). It carries its genetic blueprint as RNA. Once it infects a cell, it uses a unique enzyme called 'reverse transcriptase' to convert its RNA back into DNA, which it then seamlessly integrates into the host cell's own genome.
DECOY BUSTING: Viruses cannot divide on their own; they MUST hijack host machinery. HIV specifically targets CD4 T-cells (White Blood cells), not red blood cells. Viruses cannot survive indefinitely outside; they degrade.
EXAM INSIGHT: Because the virus's DNA hides inside the host's DNA, retroviruses are incredibly difficult to cure. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) works by blocking the reverse transcriptase enzyme.
